Are you a commercially driven Account Executive who knows how to turn opportunities into business?

Do you enjoy opening doors, engaging with senior decision-makers and building relationships that lead to long-term commercial success? Are you motivated by winning new business, taking ownership of your results and working in an international environment where your contribution makes a real difference?

Knowledge Gate Group (KGG) is looking for an ambitious Account Executive to strengthen its international sales team in Copenhagen.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of the entire sales cycle, develop your own client portfolio and work with some of the world's leading organisations within pharmaceuticals, biotechnology and life sciences.

If you combine a hunter mentality with a strategic approach to sales, we would love to hear from you.

About Knowledge Gate Group

Knowledge Gate Group is an international company connecting organisations with specialised expertise and valuable market insights.

KGG helps clients access the knowledge they need to support research, understand complex markets, develop products and make better-informed business decisions

Its clients include global pharmaceutical companies, biotech organisations, life sciences businesses and consulting firms operating in these industries.

With an international team, an entrepreneurial mindset and ambitious growth plans, KGG offers a dynamic working environment where ideas are welcomed, decisions are made quickly and employees have the opportunity to influence the company's development.

The culture is collaborative, informal and performance-driven, with a strong emphasis on individual responsibility and shared success.

The opportunity

As an Account Executive, you will play a central role in expanding KGG's international client base.

Your primary focus will be generating new business by identifying relevant organisations, understanding their challenges and connecting with decision-makers who can benefit from KGG's services.

"This is not about making hundreds of generic sales calls. It is about understanding your market, identifying the right opportunities and having meaningful commercial conversations".

You will receive support from the Business Development team and access to an initial portfolio of target companies and contacts. However, your success will depend on your ability to take initiative, conduct your own research and build a strong pipeline.

Once you win a client, the relationship remains yours. You will be responsible for developing that account, identifying additional opportunities and building long-term partnerships.

You will report directly to Lee Bourke, Head of Sales, who combines a supportive, hands-on leadership approach with clear expectations for commercial performance.

Your key responsibilities

• Identify and develop new business opportunities with international organisations.

• Build and manage your own sales pipeline through strategic prospecting and targeted outreach.

• Research potential clients, market developments and relevant buying signals.

• Engage with senior stakeholders and decision-makers across global pharmaceutical, biotech and consulting organisations.

• Manage the full sales cycle, from initial contact and discovery meetings to proposals, negotiations and closing.

• Collaborate with the BDR/SDR team to develop qualified opportunities.

• Build and maintain your own client portfolio, driving repeat business and identifying opportunities for account expansion.

• Maintain a structured approach to pipeline management, forecasting and CRM activities.

• Contribute to the development of KGG's commercial strategy and sales performance.

Who are we looking for?

• We are looking for someone who genuinely enjoys selling.

• You are ambitious, commercially curious and motivated by the opportunity to create results through your own efforts.

• You understand that successful sales require preparation, persistence and the ability to connect with different people.

• You know how to identify opportunities, ask the right questions and build credibility with experienced decision-makers.

Most importantly, you have the drive to succeed and the determination to make things happen.

We imagine that you bring:

• Proven experience in B2B sales, preferably with a strong focus on new business development.

• A track record of managing sales processes and closing deals.

• Experience in consultative selling, solution sales or knowledge-based services.

• Strong prospecting, research and business development skills.

• The confidence to communicate and negotiate with senior decision-makers.

• Experience working with a structured sales methodology.

• Excellent English communication and negotiation skills.

• A proactive, independent and results-oriented mindset.

Experience within pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or life sciences would be an advantage, but it is not a requirement.

You may come from consulting, professional services, technology, SaaS or another B2B environment.

What matters most is your commercial mindset, ability to learn and proven motivation to win new business.

Danish language skills are not required.

What makes you successful at KGG?

You are someone who:

• Takes ownership rather than waiting for opportunities to appear.

• Combines commercial ambition with curiosity and strategic thinking.

• Adapts your communication style to different personalities, cultures and stakeholders.

• Enjoys the challenge of opening new doors and winning new clients.

• Understands the value of preparation and personalised outreach.

• Thrives in an entrepreneurial environment where priorities can evolve quickly.

• Values collaboration while taking responsibility for individual results.

• You do not need to know everything about the pharmaceutical industry from day one. But you must be willing to learn, ask questions and understand your customers' businesses.

What can Knowledge Gate Group offer you?

At KGG, you will become part of an international organisation where you can have a direct impact on both your own success and the company's continued development.

You can expect:

• International exposure: Work with leading companies and senior decision-makers across global markets.

• Ownership: Build your own pipeline and develop a client portfolio that you continue to manage and grow.

• Uncapped commission: A performance-based commission structure that rewards your commercial success.

• Competitive salary: A fixed salary reflecting your experience and qualifications, combined with an attractive commission opportunity.

• Structured onboarding: Comprehensive training in KGG's services, target markets, sales processes and commercial approach.

• Supportive leadership: Work closely with an experienced Head of Sales who values trust, independence and results.

• Entrepreneurial culture: Join an international, collaborative team with direct access to management and opportunities to influence the business.

• Professional development: Strengthen your commercial capabilities while working with complex, knowledge-driven solutions.

Location and working environment

The position is based at Knowledge Gate Group's office in central Copenhagen, alternative arrangements may be discussed for the right candidates.

KGG values collaboration and prefers employees to be present in the office, particularly during onboarding. Following the probationary period, the standard arrangement is four days in the office and one day working from home.

Ready to take the next step?

If you are an ambitious Account Executive who wants to combine strategic international sales with the opportunity to build your own business portfolio, this could be your next career move.

Knowledge Gate Group has partnered with DEDIKATION to manage the recruitment process.

We encourage you to apply through the application link.

We look forward to learning more about you, your experience and what motivates you to succeed.

Apply today and become part of Knowledge Gate Group's international growth journey.

jobs.description:
Most companies that do conferencing hand you one slice of it. The desktop app, or the media pipeline, or, maybe, the join flow. Everything else you pass over a wall to another team. Not in this case. One team owns the whole path across the Airtame platform: Airtame 3, Airtame Go, Virtual Airtame, and browser, desktop, and mobile apps that go with them. The bar remains at an effortless experience. Someone walks into a room, and starts sharing. No app to hunt for, no login to chase.

The team is four engineers, and we're hiring their technical and people lead: someone who spends about 60% of time hands-on with the hardest problems, and the rest growing the engineers around them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a call you make about the streaming stack ends up in a product bolted to a wall in meeting rooms around the world. The team is small, works across disciplines, and reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Make joining a call one step that works. Today, getting an authenticated meeting started from a room takes too many turns: personal logins, manual entry, a different quirk on every platform. A year from now, starting a scheduled call on Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, or Webex should be something a room just does. Judge it by how often it works on the first try, and how rarely it reaches support.

Take the friction out of screen sharing. The browser path loses first-time users: too many clicks, not enough signposting. You'll own getting a newcomer from a short code to their screen on the wall without a stumble, and getting Miracast and AirPlay stable enough to turn on by default.

Make it behave the same everywhere. The experience varies between Airtame 3, Virtual Airtame, browser, desktop, and mobile today. By year-end, sharing and calling should feel like one product no matter which surface you're on, with real-time quality that holds up on whatever network the room happens to have.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've owned a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped building. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• Comfortable across the stack. Real-time media is second nature to you: WebRTC, streaming, the way audio and video behave over a network you don't control. You've gone deep somewhere, whether a media pipeline, native protocols, or a cross-platform client, and you can hold your own everywhere else, on browser, desktop, and mobile.

• You've made stubborn systems cooperate. Half this job is getting software to play nicely with platforms you don't own: Teams, Zoom, Meet, Webex, the operating system's own media APIs, each with its own idea of how things should go. You've done that kind of integration, and you keep your head when every platform behaves differently.

• You measure yourself by the room. Your bar is the person standing at the "share" button. Someone who's never seen an Airtame, getting their screen up first try with no help. That's what you optimize for, and it steers the calls you make when something has to give.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• The defining calls are still ahead. Airtame's collaboration software keeps spreading across more devices and form factors, so the shape of the next phase is still open, and you'd be the one setting it.

• At our size, a major call you make shows up in front of customers within weeks, so the feedback comes back fast.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Significant responsibility and ownership over projects and your field of expertise.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

****What Our Employment Decisions Are NOT Based On

****Race, colour, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, disability, ethnicity, national origin, marital status, family or parental status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other legally protected classification or status. And we will not tolerate discrimination or harassment.

****What Our Employment Decisions ARE Based On

****Business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, and candidates potential for growing with Airtame.

****How We Handle Your Application Data

****Airtame ApS (CVR 35478973, Copenhagen), together with Airtame US Inc. for US roles, processes the information you submit to assess your application. We do this under the EU General Data Protection Regulation, wherever you are based. Your data is stored in Greenhouse, our recruiting system, which may store it outside the EU under standard EU safeguards. Only the people involved in hiring can see it. For roles with privileged access to our systems, we’ll contact one professional reference or previous employer that you name, to confirm your role and dates. We’ll tell you before we do. We keep your data for 6 months after the recruitment process ends, or longer where US law requires it or where you consent to us keeping it for future roles. To get a copy of your data, correct or delete it, or object to how we use it, write to data@airtame.com. You can also complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency (Datatilsynet).

****Business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, and candidates potential for growing with Airtame.

Marketing Automation Manager

Are you a hands-on Marketing Automation Manager who enjoys turning customer data into personalised experiences and measurable business results?

As part of our E-commerce & Digital Transformation team, you will drive the development and optimisation of our marketing automation activities.

You will work hands-on in Bloomreach (CDP & Marketing Automation) and HubSpot (CRM), designing and optimising automated customer journeys, activating customer data, and identifying new opportunities to improve customer experiences and commercial performance. Email content and production are handled by colleagues, allowing you to focus on marketing automation, segmentation, and personalisation.

You will also take ownership of our marketing automation roadmap, prioritising initiatives based on customer needs, business impact, and available resources.

The role involves close collaboration with colleagues across E-commerce, Marketing, IT, and external partners.

• Own and develop the marketing automation roadmap, prioritising customer journeys and commercial impact across B2C and B2B.

• Design and optimise personalised, automated customer journeys in Bloomreach and HubSpot to drive engagement, retention, and repeat bookings.

• Activate customer data through segmentation and behavioural triggers to improve customer journeys across email, app, sms, website, and MyScandlines.

You are an experienced marketing automation professional who combines strong technical skills with an analytical and commercial mindset.

You enjoy working directly in the platforms, but you also see the bigger picture and take responsibility for driving initiatives forward.

We expect that you:

• Have 4+ years of hands-on experience with marketing automation or CRM, either in-house or at an agency.

• Have solid experience with Bloomreach or similar platforms, such as Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, or Iterable.

• Ideally have experience with HubSpot, although this is not a requirement.

• Have strong experience with automated customer journeys, advanced segmentation, personalisation, and lifecycle marketing.

• Are comfortable working with customer data, reporting, performance metrics, and A/B testing.

• Understand CRM structures, workflows, lead management, and customer data integration.

You are proactive, structured, and solution-oriented, with a natural ability to take ownership and drive initiatives forward.

Most importantly, you combine strategic thinking with a hands-on approach and are motivated by turning ideas into meaningful results.

We offer an exciting and challenging role in a dynamic, international organisation with high ambitions. You will join a digital and commercial team of dedicated colleagues in an informal working environment.

Senior Manager, Application Operations – Aarhus

Do you want to lead the team that keeps Systematic applications running around the clock, while developing a team of 12–14 specialists and bringing Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices into their daily work?

The job

You will lead the Application Operations team in Customer Operations and report to the Director of Customer Operations. The team keeps customer-facing and internal applications secure, reliable and available, and you will set the direction, develop your people and make sure we meet our service commitments.

Your role combines classic operations with the growth of our cloud offering, so you will balance daily delivery with building something new. You will also take on a growing responsibility for handling security incidents in cooperation with our security lead.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Leading and mentoring 12–14 team members through regular 1:1s and performance reviews

• Supporting incident response and coordinating deployment schedules and change management

• Introducing SRE practices such as SLOs, error budgets, blameless post-incident reviews and toil reduction

• Driving automation, capacity planning and operational KPIs together with development and infrastructure teams

• Managing the team budget, time registration and on-call payout calculations

Joining the team

Our site reliability engineers (SREs) work with system administration, DevOps support, monitoring and technical support to the business units, and we run in a 24/7 environment with rotating on-call schedules. You will work closely with development teams, infrastructure teams and customer support, so that solutions like Columna stay available for the clinicians and care staff who depend on them every day.

Your qualifications

• 7–10 years of experience in application operations, system administration, DevOps or SRE roles either as a technical profile or a manager.

• 3–5 years of experience leading technical teams

• Experience being responsible for technical deliveries with full ownership of operations and management responsibility

• Commercial understanding of contracts, budgets, and service and delivery agreements

• Experience negotiating service agreements with internal business units as a professional partner

• Experience handling security incidents and helping business units restore services quickly

• Experience with high-availability, 24/7 operational environments

• Proficiency with monitoring and observability tools, and experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure or GCP)

• Understanding of containerisation and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and CI/CD pipelines

• Proficiency with ITIL or similar operational frameworks, and a solid understanding of SRE principles

Your everyday job will have many contact point with people inside and outside the department so we are looking for a manager with a extrovert personality who is keen to create strong relationships.

You look beyond your own department and understand how Systematic's business works, and you turn strategy into action while explaining it clearly to others. You balance technical depth with the overview a manager needs, and you are comfortable taking calculated commercial risks.

Part of the role is to grow our cloud offering and make it clear and easy to communicate, and you stay committed for the long term, from the first launch to stable daily delivery. You lead through influence and expertise, you explain technical topics to non-technical stakeholders, and you stay calm during incidents.

You need fluent written and spoken English. Travel is minimal (0–10% a year), and you will occasionally be available outside office hours for incidents or maintenance windows.

Do you want to work with the full development cycle, from customer requirements to tested, tailored software, in a defence team where quality matters? Join our Bespoke team in Aarhus and build the extensions our customers need.

The job

In this role, you will help deliver customised add-ons, integrations and extensions to Systematic’s defence product suite, across the full development cycle – from analysing requirements and designing solutions to implementing, testing and troubleshooting them – and help continually improving the way we work.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you passionate about understanding how offshore wind turbines respond to the forces of nature? Do you want to use your engineering expertise to influence the design, performance and long-term reliability of offshore wind farms?

At Vattenfall, we believe there is a way to build a more sustainable energy future. We're looking for a Senior Offshore Wind Turbine Loads & Structural Dynamics Engineer to join our Structural Loads team within Offshore Engineering.

In this specialist role, you'll work at the heart of offshore wind turbine engineering, using engineering analysis, aeroelastic modelling and measurement data to investigate complex turbine behaviour and turn the results into sound engineering decisions.

From early development and turbine selection through to operational optimisation and lifetime extension, your expertise will help shape important technical decisions across our offshore wind portfolio.

You'll join an international team of engineering specialists who value collaboration, technical excellence and finding practical solutions to complex challenges.

Your Role

As a Senior Offshore Wind Turbine Loads & Structural Dynamics Engineer, you'll combine hands-on technical expertise with responsibility for delivering complex engineering work across offshore wind projects and operating assets.

Working closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams, turbine manufacturers and external partners, you'll help ensure our offshore wind turbines are designed and operated safely, efficiently and reliably.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Advanced engineering analysis: Independently define, perform and technically own aeroelastic load analyses, including modelling strategy, execution, validation and interpretation, turning complex results into sound engineering conclusions and decisions.

• Structural integrity: Assess wind turbine and support-structure loading and independently investigate and resolve complex engineering questions relating to fatigue, structural performance and lifetime extension.

• Project delivery: Technically lead load-related engineering activities, ensuring technical deliverables meet project requirements, quality standards and deadlines, and act as the Structural Loads technical point of contact for assigned projects.

• Technical collaboration: Work closely with specialists across Wind Turbine Engineering, Primary Structures, Geotechnical Engineering and Metocean to solve multidisciplinary engineering problems where turbine loads, structural response and environmental conditions interact.

• Stakeholder engagement: Act as a trusted technical partner to internal stakeholders, understanding their needs and translating complex loads-related questions, risks and results into clear engineering recommendations that support project decisions.

• Innovation and improvement: Develop and refine simulation models, engineering tools and analysis methods to improve turbine performance, reduce technical risks and support continuous improvement.

Your Profile

We're looking for an experienced engineering specialist who can independently investigate and solve complex engineering problems, translating detailed analysis into well-founded engineering conclusions and practical solutions.

You'll bring a strong understanding of wind turbine aeroelasticity and structural dynamics, alongside the ability to take technical ownership, exercise sound engineering judgement and communicate complex technical matters clearly and effectively across different disciplines.

Qualifications

• A master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Wind Energy or a closely related discipline.

• At least 7 years of relevant industry experience in wind turbine aeroelasticity, load simulation or structural dynamics.

• Extensive hands-on experience defining and performing aeroelastic load analyses, including model development, simulation, validation, post-processing and interpretation of results.

• Strong knowledge of wind turbine aerodynamics, structural dynamics, control systems and load-generation mechanisms.

• Experience interpreting simulation results, validating engineering models and working with measurement data.

• Experience working within multidisciplinary engineering environments, ideally within offshore wind, turbine manufacturing or renewable energy development.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical findings and collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

• Professional proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

It would also be beneficial if you have experience in:

• Offshore wind turbine foundation design, hydrodynamics or coupled turbine-foundation analysis.

• Relevant IEC and DNV standards and certification processes.

• Engineering programming tools such as Python or MATLAB.

• Operational load assessments, turbine power upgrades or lifetime extension projects.

Above all, you'll bring curiosity, a careful and structured approach to engineering challenges, and a genuine interest in sharing knowledge and developing solutions together.

Oxfam is one of the world’s largest development and humanitarian organisations, and our analyses and messages are heard by global leaders and in the Danish debate. Read more in Oxfam Denmark’s strategy here and see the full function description on this page.

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

**Knowing when it’s good enough

**We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

**Knowing when to slow down

**Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

**Make time to experiment

**We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.
